title: Screens to review
lede: The new screens are on the test site with sample data for a made-up community; nothing you click there is saved. Open a screen, step through its Demo states, then answer here: Yes to build it as shown, Change with a sentence on what should be different, or Discuss to talk it through on the next call.
howTo: On each screen, the Demo state control at the top steps through every situation the screen has to handle. A few screens have a side switch too, because two different people see them. Please look at every state: the awkward cases are where the design earns its keep.

features.title: Bringing a community in
features.intro: How a board gets its properties, owners and opening balances into HOAhx from its own spreadsheet, and how it sees residents join.

screens.title: Upload the spreadsheet and match the columns
screens.look: The board uploads its own CSV or Excel file. HOAhx suggests which column is which; a person confirms or corrects every suggestion. The messy file and the second import are the states to linger on.

screens.title: Check it before it goes in
screens.look: Rows ready, rows needing a decision, rows that cannot go in. A duplicate, a missing detail and a value that only looks wrong are treated as three different things; only a blocked row stops the import.

screens.title: Opening balances: the treasurer signs off
screens.look: The total of all opening balances next to the figure the treasurer expected. Nothing is saved until the treasurer approves it, possibly a different person on a different day.

screens.title: What past imports did, and fixing one
screens.look: Every import on record: who ran it, what it added or changed, and how a mistake is corrected with the correction kept on record.

screens.title: Who has joined
screens.look: Every home and person against the four steps, invited, joined, verified, active; whose invitation has lapsed; sending again to one person or to everyone not yet joined.

screens.title: Someone joined without an invitation
screens.look: What the board sees when a person claims a home without a link, and the plain "we are checking" screen that person sees, ending with the offer of automatic payments.
